Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu makes landfall near Ongole in Prakasam district of Andhra Pradesh early this morning. The Storm brought heavy rainfall across South Coastal Andhra Pradesh, impacting districts including Prakasam, Bapatla, Palnadu, SPSR Nellore, and parts of adjoining states. Gale-force winds reaching speeds of 100 to 110 km per hour, gusting up to 120 km per hour, are moving along and off the South Andhra Pradesh coast. A storm surge of 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide is likely to inundate low-lying areas of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh, with the maximum peak surge expected over Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts. Residents in Prakasam and other affected districts can reach out to the dedicated disaster support line, Mana Mitra, at 9552300009 for assistance or to report emergencies.

 

Heavy rainfall is being reported across parts of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla, Palnadu, Guntur, Krishna, NTR, Eluru and West Godavari districts are among the affected areas. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also forecast in parts of Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema during the next 12 hours.Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the situation with officials and district collectors. He directed them to ensure public safety and prevent loss of life and property. Fallen trees in several areas have been cleared. People living in unsafe areas have been shifted to relief camps. Schools and colleges have been closed in four districts. Emergency and relief teams are on alert. The South Coast Railway has opened round-the-clock control rooms. People are advised to remain indoors, avoid unnecessary travel and follow official warnings.Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu’s impact is being felt in southern Odisha following its landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast. Heavy rainfall is forecast in several districts, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri. Odisha Government has intensified evacuation and disaster preparedness measures, focusing especially on flood-affected and vulnerable areas.

 

Southern Odisha is bracing for another spell of heavy rainfall following Cyclone Murasu’s landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast. Rainfall activity is expected to continue across several districts, with the IMD forecasting heavy to very heavy rain in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri. The fresh spell of rain has heightened concerns in areas still recovering from recent floods. The Odisha Government has identified vulnerable locations and intensified evacuation to safer places. Around one lakh sixty thousand people have been shifted, while district collectors and emergency response teams remain on high alert. The administration is also closely monitoring rivers, reservoirs and landslide-prone areas to prevent any loss of life. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

In Tamil Nadu, moderate rain has been reported in many parts of north coastal districts including Tiruvallur Chennai and Kanchipuram.  As Murasu has crossed Andhra coast near northern Tamil Nadu more rain is expected in northern districts of the state.

 

 

Murasu cyclone has not created havoc in Chennai and Tiruvallur. Even though heavy rain was forecast in northern districts of the state Chennai has escaped the fury of cyclone effect. It is cloudy in Chennai. People were not allowed to go near the Besant Nagar Beach for safety reasons as sea waves rose sharply. Met office regional director Dr V R Durai said that Murasu cyclone may not bring heavy rain in Chennai and neighbouring districts. However certain parts of Cuddalore is having heavy rain.  K Devi Padmanabhan Akashwani News Chennai.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune Metro projects worth around 21 thousand 800 crore rupees through video conferencing this afternoon. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. More from our correspondent:

 

“Hinjewadi maan – shivajinagr metro line that is ‘Puneri Metro’ or the ‘Pink Line’, is expected to benefit IT professionals working at Hinjewadi IT Park. The metro corridor is approximately 23 kilometres long and has a total of 23 stations. Passenger services will initially begin at 17 stations in the first phase. One of the key features of this project is that around 100 women train pilots will operate the metro. Women will also make up nearly 50 per cent of the total staff deployed at the metro stations. Several measures have also been taken to promote environmental sustainability. Around 30 per cent of the project’s electricity requirements will be met through renewable energy. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will also virtually lay the foundation stones for Vanaz to Chandni Chowk, Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi, Kharadi to Khadakwasla and Nal Stop to Manik Baug metro line. The project represents an important step towards strengthening Pune’s urban mobility infrastructure through technological innovation and modern transportation solutions. Madhavi Kulkarni, Akashvani News, Pune.”

The government has notified a new set of rules governing India’s civil aviation sector, replacing the nearly nine-decade-old Aircraft Rules, 1937. The new rules called the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, will come into effect on 1st of January, next year. The rules provide the regulatory framework on various aspects of the aviation sector including aircraft registration, manufacturing, safety certification, maintenance, flight operations, personnel licensing and airport operations.

 

Airlines operating scheduled air services are required to determine fares based on factors such as operating costs and submit tariff details to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). The provision allows the Centre to issue written directions if it determines that an extraordinary situation has arisen and intervention is necessary in the public interest. The new rules also mandate greater transparency in airfare pricing, requiring airlines to publish their fares on official websites and other digital platforms. The DGCA will continue to monitor tariffs set by scheduled airlines. One of the key areas covered by the rules is the registration and certification of aircraft. They specify requirements for registering aircraft in India and obtaining certificates that establish whether an aircraft is safe to fly.

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has reviewed preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in 18 districts across four divisions and directed senior officials to strengthen voter lists, security arrangements and personnel training to ensure free, fair and peaceful polling.

The review meeting was chaired by Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg in Meerut in the presence of Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa and other senior commission officials, according to a statement issued by the CEO’s office.

 

Mr Garg emphasised the importance of the review for both first-time district election officers and police chiefs and experienced officials, noting that election rules and guidelines undergo periodic changes. He urged all officials to examine the issues discussed afresh and improve their preparations accordingly.

 

He also stressed ensuring minimum assured facilities at polling stations and launching EVM awareness programmes. The senior deputy election commissioner instructed authorities to maintain strict surveillance against the illegal transportation and distribution of liquor during the elections, including checks at distilleries’ source and exit points.

 

He also called for effective arrangements for mobile phone deposit boxes at polling stations on polling day, with the assistance of volunteers. Officials were asked to ensure training for state-level master trainers and familiarise relevant personnel with postal ballot-related instructions.

 

Rinwa directed officials to launch special drives in classes 11 and 12 and degree colleges to enrol young people becoming eligible to vote for the first time. He also asked authorities to re-examine rejected Form 6 applications to ensure that eligible citizens are included in electoral rolls.

 

Applicants filling Form 6 should provide their mobile numbers and complete addresses accurately, while Common Service Centre operators should be trained immediately in the online application process and measures to prevent multiple entries. The CEO further directed district election officers to recheck all Forms 6, 7 and 8 entered by computer assistants since the conclusion of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The CEO also directed officials to ensure distribution of voter information slips five days before polling and record the distribution in booth-level officers’ registers.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has congratulated the Indian Navy for successfully executing a meticulously coordinated 48-hour operation to rescue all 20 crew members of the pirated fishing vessel, Azini in the Arabian Sea. In a social media post, the Defence Minister said that the brave personnel have once again demonstrated the country’s ability, intent and resolve to safeguard lives, uphold maritime security and ensure stability across the Indian Ocean Region. Mr Singh said that the swift localisation, interception and safe release of the crew and vessel from significantly-armed pirates, with timely support from the Indian Air Force, speak well of the Indian Navy’s high operational readiness and ability to respond decisively to maritime threats across the region. He added, India continues to stand resolute in ensuring SAFE SEAS and a free, open and secure Indian Ocean Region.

The midterm elections in the United States will be held today. Americans will vote for all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships.

 

The poll will decide whether Republicans retain control of Congress or Democrats win back one or both chambers during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term. The voting will start and close at different times across the United States, with results expected to begin coming in as votes are counted. The outcome of the midterm poll will decide which political party – Trump’s Republicans or opposition Democrats – controls Congress and how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans. Apart from the ongoing war between the United States and Iran, the state of US economy remains a key issue for voters ahead of the midterm elections. Immigration is another key issue with Republicans saying Trump has delivered on a major campaign pledge in 2024 by tightening the border and launching a widespread crackdown on illegal immigration. YASHASVI KIRYA FOR AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI

Indian Men’s Hockey Team completed an unbeaten league-stage run at the Asian Champions Trophy 2026 yesterday with an 8-0 win over Korea – their fifth in a row in Jalandhar. India finished at the top of the standings with five wins from five matches and will face Korea again in the semi-finals as the tournament moves to Mohali, where the semis will be played tomorrow and the medal matches on Thursday. Second-placed Japan will face Malaysia, who finished the league stage in third place, in the other semi-final. India finished with 15 points and a goal difference of +29. Japan ended second with 10 points, followed by Malaysia with nine and Korea with six points.

 

“Indian Men’s kept the momentum throughout the match in front of a jubilant packed house. In the first quarter, they hit 3 goals and then carried on to hit rest of the five in the remaining time. Dilpreet Singh scored twice, while six others including Captain Harmanpreet Singh hit the remaining goals. Out of the total, 3 were converted from Penalty Corners and 5 were Field Goals. With this dominated win, India finished at the top of the standings with five wins from as many matches.


Today is rest day. India will face Korea again in the semi-finals as the tournament will now move to Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium at Mohali, where the semis will be played on November 4th and the medal matches on November 5th. In another semi-final, second-placed Japan will face Malaysia, who finished the league stage at the third place. Rajesh Bali, Akashvani News, Jalandhar.”

In badminton, veteran Indian shuttler HS Prannoy and emerging women’s singles player Tanvi Sharma will lead a depleted Indian contingent at the Korea Open 2026, with several of the country’s top players opting out of the BWF Super 500 tournament beginning today in South Korea. India will be without two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu, men’s doubles stars Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, and the ace men’s singles shuttler Lakshya Sen. Prannoy will be India’s sole representative in the men’s singles after Sen’s withdrawal. The former world No. 6, currently ranked 38th, will open his campaign against South Korea’s Asian Games bronze medallist Yoo Tae-bin. In the women’s singles, Tanvi Sharma and Anmol Kharb will carry India’s hopes in the main draw. Malvika Bansod and Ashmita Chaliha, were also part of the women’s singles draw but have withdrawn from the competition. India’s men’s doubles representation will be limited to Arjun Reddy Pochana and Achutaditya Rao Doddavarapu, who will begin their campaign in the qualifying rounds. In women’s doubles, Ritika Thaker and Sonali Singh will represent India, while Dhruv Rawat and Maneesha K will compete in the mixed doubles main draw.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The four-day Summit will be held till 5th of this month. The theme of the Summit is ‘Invest Innovate Inspire’. More from our correspondent:

“The Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 will attract participants from over 130 countries, including more than 40 Ministers, along with policymakers, investors, financial institutions and industry leaders. It will serve as a global platform for clean energy investment, industry engagement and technology partnerships. The Summit is witnessing the participation from Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom as Country Partners. The Summit is being held alongside the 9th Session of the International Solar Alliance Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen. The Summit will also host plenary sessions, ministerial discussions, and government-to-government engagements to promote investment, partnerships and project development.  Meanwhile, the Expo will feature over 400 exhibitors showcasing advanced technologies, Indian manufacturing capabilities and clean energy solutions across solar and wind power, green hydrogen, energy storage and other emerging areas. A CBI team has successfully extradited Sourabh Chandrakar, the promoter and mastermind behind the 6,000-crore rupees Mahadev Online Book illegal betting syndicate, from Oman to India. Following an Interpol Red Corner Notice, Chandrakar was located and detained by the Royal Oman Police. A CBI team flew to Muscat, Oman, to escort him back. He will be produced before the special CBI Court at Raipur in Chhattisgarh today. Chandrakar faces severe criminal charges stemming from separate probes launched at the request of the Chhattisgarh government. He is named as a principal accused across two filed chargesheets detailing criminal conspiracy, cheating, forgery, and public servant bribery under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Chhattisgarh Gambling (Prohibition) Act.

The deep depression over Bay of Bengal has intensified into cyclonic storm Murasu. India Meteorological Department (IMD) said, Murasu is likely to make landfall along Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, in early hours tomorrow as a severe cyclonic storm. IMD said, wind speed of the cyclonic storm is likely to be between 80 and 90 km per hour, with occasional gusts up to 100 km per hour. Met Department has advised fishermen not to venture into Southeast Bay of Bengal till today and into Southwest Bay of Bengal till Wednesday morning. Weather Agency also predicted thunderstorm accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Konkan, Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh during the next two days.

Andhra Pradesh is bracing for the impact of Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu, which is moving towards the south coast. The State government has stepped up precautionary measures and put rescue and relief teams on alert. More from our correspondent:

“Cyclonic Storm Murasu over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. It is likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole, around midnight tonight and early hours of tomorrow. Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is expected today and tomorrow in Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Markapuram and Nellore districts, besides other parts of south coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu spoke to the Tamil Nadu and Karnataka Chief Ministers, seeking personnel and machinery for power restoration. Both assured assistance. Six NDRF and seven SDRF teams are ready for rescue operations. Control rooms have been set up. People have been advised to stay alert and follow the instructions issued by the authorities. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu over the Bay of Bengal is moving towards the south Andhra Pradesh coast, threatening heavy to very heavy rainfall over southern Odisha. The IMD has forecast increased rainfall activity over the state during the next two days, particularly tomorrow and the day after. Odisha Government has stepped up precautionary measures as flood-affected districts brace for another spell of heavy rain. More from our Correspondent:

“Rain has already started in parts of southern Odisha. The IMD has issued yellow warnings for 19 districts today, including Ganjam and Gajapati, while five southern districts have an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall tomorrow and the day after. The state is not expected to face a direct landfall, but heavy rainfall and gusty winds are likely. The government has identified vulnerable areas, initiated evacuation and placed district administrations on high alert. Balimela reservoir gates have also been opened as a precaution. Fresh rainfall could aggravate flooding, trigger landslides and disrupt connectivity in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal, which are still recovering from recent floods. Rainfall is likely to gradually subside starting Thursday. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

The country’s gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections grew nearly 23 per cent year-on-year to over two lakh 31 thousand crore rupees in October this year, driven by robust domestic economic activity and a sharp rise in tax revenue from imports. According to the provisional government data, gross GST revenue from domestic sales climbed 15.8 per cent year-on-year to over 1.59 lakh crore rupees in October, while revenue from imports surged 42.2 per cent to 72 thousand 246 crore rupees. The gross GST revenue collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42 thousand 935 crore rupees, State GST of 51 thousand 340 crore rupees and Integrated GST of 1 lakh 37 thousand 15 crore rupees.

Being organised by the Jammu and Kashmir Trade Promotion Organisation, the event will feature products under the One District One Product initiative, highlighting the unique offerings of different districts and promoting locally manufactured and traditional products. More from our correspondent:

“The exhibition aims to provide greater visibility to local entrepreneurs, artisans and businesses while encouraging people to support homegrown products. Authentic Dogri cuisine will be another major attraction, giving visitors an opportunity to experience the traditional flavours of the Jammu region. Cultural performances will further add to the event, celebrating the diverse traditions and artistic heritage of Jammu and Kashmir. The expo will also highlight the contribution of rural women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs), providing them with a platform to showcase their products and connect with potential customers. Their participation is expected to bring attention to grassroots entrepreneurship and the role of women in strengthening local livelihoods. By bringing together crafts, cuisine, cultural performances and locally produced goods, Jammu Expo 2.0 aims to create a platform for cultural exchange, business promotion and community participation. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved Northern Bullet Train Corridor which will connect Delhi to Guwahati via Siliguri. This was disclosed by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw in Varanasi yesterday. The Minister was in the city to flag off Varanasi-New Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper Express. The Northern Bullet Train Corridor will cover approximately 1,500 km and will pass through key cities across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal before extending into Assam. The key stations include Delhi, Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow, Ayodhya, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Patna, Siliguri, and Guwahati. Mr Vaishnaw said, Northern Bullet Train Corridor aims to revolutionize connectivity across northern and eastern India, cutting down the current 20-hour journey between Delhi and Siliguri to just six hours.

The Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Train will be inaugurated today. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will flag off the train from Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal in Bengaluru, Karnataka. The new Vande Bharat Sleeper train will cover the journey between Bengaluru and Mumbai in around 16 hours, offering passengers a comfortable overnight travel experience with modern amenities and advanced safety features. The train will run six days a week, except Mondays from Bengaluru and Tuesdays from Mumbai. It will stop at Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Yadgir, Kalaburagi, Solapur, Pune and Kalyan. More from our correspondent:

 

“The Vande Bharat Sleeper train between Bengaluru and Mumbai is designed to make overnight journeys more comfortable and convenient. The train offers First AC, AC Two-Tier and AC Three-Tier accommodation, with cushioned berths, integrated reading lights, mobile charging points and ample luggage space. Passengers will also benefit from touch-free bio-vacuum toilets, automatic doors, onboard infotainment and GPS-based passenger information displays. First AC coaches will additionally offer hot-water shower facilities. For passenger safety, the train is equipped with CCTV cameras, fire detection systems and emergency communication facilities. With modern amenities and enhanced safety features, the new service aims to make overnight travel between Bengaluru and Mumbai more comfortable and convenient. ANKIT KUMAR, AKASHVANI NEWS, BENGALURU.”

President Droupadi Murmu will attend the state-level Haryana Day celebrations in Kurukshetra today, marking the 60th anniversary of the formation of Haryana. The main function will be held at Kurukshetra University. The President will inaugurate an exhibition showcasing Haryana’s six-decade journey since its formation in 1966. The liftoff will take place from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. Cyclone Arnab has caused extensive damage to crops, houses, roads and power infrastructure across several districts of Andhra Pradesh. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has requested the Centre to send an inter-ministerial team for an early assessment of the losses. The State Government has intensified relief and restoration operations in the affected areas. More from our correspondent:

 

“Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed cyclone relief operations through the State’s Real-Time Governance Centre and directed officials to expedite restoration of essential services. Officials are also clearing blocked roads and restoring drinking water supplies. Meanwhile, the Chief Minister has requested Centre to send a team to assess cyclone-related losses. R. The US Federal Reserve has kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%, keeping the average effective rate at approximately 3.9%. More from our correspondent:

 

“Led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) opted to maintain the status quo following a quarter-percentage-point hike in September, which had marked the central bank’s first interest rate increase in three years. The decision was not unanimous. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented from the hold, voting to raise the target range by a quarter percentage point due to persistent inflation concerns. The central bank stated that keeping rates unchanged allows for the “accumulation of more information” to ensure a timely return of inflation to its 2% target. The decision comes less than a week before the US midterm elections. Financial markets and economists continue to anticipate a potential final quarter-point rate hike at the next FOMC meeting scheduled for 8th and 9th December 2026. KAUMUDEE PAREEK, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

The very severe cyclonic storm Arnab has commenced its landfall process along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts near Kakinada. According to India Meteorological Department (IMD), the landfall process started at 1:20 AM today. The crossing began earlier than originally expected due to the rapid movement of the storm. The storm hit the coast packing sustained maximum wind speeds of 115-125 km per hour, with gusts reaching up to 140 km per hour.

 

Heavy rainfall and strong winds have disrupted normal life across several coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh.

 

“Cyclone Arnab remained practically stationary near the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts, south of Yanam. Extremely heavy rainfall has lashed several coastal districts, with Kannuripalem in Anakapalli district recording 259 millimetres of rainfall. Strong winds reaching 130 kilometres per hour were recorded at Maruteru, while uprooted trees, power disruptions and flooding have affected normal life in several areas. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewing relief operations with district collectors and disaster management officials. More than 84 thousand people have been evacuated to 290 relief shelters, while NDRF teams remain deployed in affected areas. Train and flight services have been disrupted, with several cancellations and rescheduling of services. Authorities have warned of storm surges up to two-and-a-half metres, particularly near Kakinada and Yanam, and advised residents of vulnerable coastal and low-lying areas to remain alert. R. Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

Puducherry Public Works Minister Malladi Krishna Rao and Regional Administrator Sivaraj Meena visited the affected areas  and assured residents of all necessary assistance. With K Sheshu Babu, Bibin S Nath, Akashvani News, Puducherry.”

Parliamentary election in Israel remained deadlocked, with exit polls from all three major television networks giving opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc a narrow two-seat lead over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp. The projections put Eisenkot’s bloc at 52 seats and Netanyahu’s Likud-led alliance at 50, leaving neither side with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament-Knesset.

 

“The results could give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, but his path to power remains uncertain. The remaining 18 seats were projected to go to Arab parties not aligned with either bloc, and Eisenkot has largely ruled out forming a government with them. Netanyahu, meanwhile, could remain caretaker prime minister if coalition talks fail.

 

Israel’s Central Elections Committee said, voters turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades and around seven percentage points above the 2022 election. The vote was the first since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

 

Netanyahu has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents removed him from office only once since 2009, but he returned to power 18 months later.

With the latest exit polls showing a narrow advantage for Eisenkot’s bloc but no clear majority for either side, the final count and subsequent coalition negotiations will determine who can form Israel’s next government. Kaumudee Pareek, Akashvani News.”
